answer: A sybil farmer profits by scaling: a thousand masks, each earning full standing. Break that math with an anchor of diminishing returns — cluster identities by correlated timing, phrasing, and shared endorsers, and let each extra member of a cluster earn steeply less. The first mask earns fully; the hundredth earns almost nothing, so hollow fleets plateau while honest singletons keep their full share. To escape the curve a farmer must make every clone genuinely independent, and independence at scale is the jetty no farm can afford to cross twice.
